en.name: Sherbet and sorbet
en.summary: Sherbet and sorbet keep 9 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe well beyond that — what runs out is texture, because these have little or no fat to hold the structure and go icy faster than ice cream does.
en.pantry: No room-temperature storage. A sorbet is fruit purée, sugar and water with almost no fat, and once it starts melting there is nothing holding it together — it goes to syrup quickly and will ferment in a warm kitchen. Sherbet contains a little dairy, which brings it closer to ice cream in how it should be handled. Take the tub out for a few minutes only, or use a warm scoop, rather than leaving it on the counter.
en.fridge: Refrigerating sherbet or sorbet is not recommended, and no refrigerated timeline is given. At fridge temperature it is simply melting, and a melted sorbet that is refrozen sets into a solid, sweet block of ice rather than anything scoopable: the tiny ice crystals that make a good sorbet only form while it is being churned. If you want it softer, move the tub somewhere less cold in the freezer for a while, never to the fridge.
en.freezer: 9 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously at −18 °C it stays safe indefinitely; the window is about texture. With little or no fat to interrupt them, ice crystals grow readily with every temperature swing, so the door of the freezer is the worst possible place for a tub. Keep it at the back, press baking paper onto the surface of a part-eaten tub before replacing the lid, and expect a fruit sorbet to lose its bright colour and aroma before it loses anything else.
en.thawing: Do not thaw — soften. A few minutes at room temperature, or a scoop dipped in hot water, is all it needs. A tub that has melted right through should be thrown away rather than refrozen.
spoilage: A hard, solid, glassy block instead of a scoopable texture — it melted and refroze.
A thick crust of ice crystals over the surface.
Colour faded from bright fruit to dull, and a flat aroma.
A fermented or alcoholic smell, meaning it thawed at some point.
tips: Keep the tub at the back of the freezer, never in the door.
Press baking paper onto the surface before replacing the lid.
Soften with a warm scoop rather than leaving the tub out.
Sorbet loses colour and aroma before it loses texture — buy tubs you will finish.

faq.q: How long does sorbet last in the freezer?
faq.a: 9 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe beyond that, but it turns icy and the fruit flavour fades.
It is not recommended. It sets into a solid block of ice rather than a scoopable sorbet, because the fine crystals only form during churning.

faq.q: Why does sorbet go icy faster than ice cream?
faq.a: Because it has little or no fat to interrupt the ice crystals. Every temperature swing lets them grow, and there is nothing in the mix to stop them.

zh.name: 雪酪與冰沙
zh.summary: 雪酪與冰沙在 −18 °C 下自購買日起可保有最佳品質 9 個月。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全——先用完的是口感：它幾乎沒有油脂撐住結構，所以會比冰淇淋更快變得冰碴。
zh.pantry: 沒有室溫保存這一項。sorbet 是果泥、糖和水，幾乎不含油脂，一旦開始融化就沒有東西撐得住它——它很快化成糖水，在溫暖的廚房裡還會發酵。sherbet 含少量乳製品，處理方式要更接近冰淇淋。請只拿出來幾分鐘，或把挖杓溫熱一下，不要整桶擺在檯面上等它軟。
zh.fridge: 不建議把雪酪或冰沙放冷藏，這裡也不給冷藏期限。在冷藏溫度下它就只是在融化；而融化過再凍回去的雪酪會變成一塊實心的甜冰，根本挖不動：讓雪酪好吃的那些細小冰晶，只有在攪打過程中才會形成。想要它軟一點，就把整桶移到冷凍庫裡沒那麼冷的位置放一會兒，絕對不是移到冷藏。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下自購買日起 9 個月品質最好。全程維持在 −18 °C 就一直是安全的；這個期限講的是口感。因為幾乎沒有油脂去打斷冰晶，只要溫度一波動冰晶就長大，所以冷凍櫃門邊是最糟的位置。請放深處；吃剩的那桶蓋回蓋子前先在表面壓一張烘焙紙。另外，水果雪酪通常在口感壞掉之前，就先失去鮮亮的顏色和香氣了。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍，是回軟。在室溫放幾分鐘，或把挖杓泡一下熱水，這樣就夠了。已經整桶融透的請丟掉，不要再凍回去。
spoilage: 變成又硬又實、像玻璃一樣的冰塊，完全挖不動——它融化過又再結凍。
表面結了厚厚一層冰晶。
顏色從鮮亮的水果色褪成暗沉，香氣也變得扁平。
聞起來發酵或有酒精味，表示它在某個時候解凍過。
tips: 整桶放冷凍櫃深處，絕對不要放門邊。
蓋回蓋子前先在表面壓一張烘焙紙。
用溫熱的挖杓讓它好挖，不要整桶擺在外面。
雪酪會先失去顏色和香氣、才失去口感——買吃得完的份量。

faq.a: −18 °C 下自購買日起 9 個月品質最好。只要沒退冰放更久仍然安全，但會變冰碴、果香也會褪。

faq.q: 融化的雪酪可以再冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 不建議。它會凍成一塊挖不動的實心冰，因為那些細緻的冰晶只有在攪打時才形成。

faq.q: 雪酪為什麼比冰淇淋更快變冰碴？
faq.a: 因為它幾乎沒有油脂去打斷冰晶。每次溫度波動冰晶就長大，而配方裡沒有東西擋得住。
